correctness.rationale: Centering the sole critical point and sending its image to zero gives a degree-n proper map with a zero of multiplicity n, hence a rotation of z^n. Undoing the range change and absorbing rotations gives the canonical family with a the modulus of the critical value. Input automorphisms preserve the weighted derivative. Direct differentiation and angular minimization of |1−az^n| give the radial profile and all angular equality cases. Its stationary parameter decreases from 1 to 0 and the radial profile vanishes at both ends, so the maximizing radius is unique. In t=e^(−s) the profile factors into a strictly increasing positive factor and the Schwarz–Pick bracket; the maximum is at t>a (the derivative in t at t=a is positive for a>0). Thus the partial derivative in a at the maximum is positive. The factor n sinh(s/n) strictly decreases with n and dominates s. The small-s and large-s bounds from the n=2 profile give compactness of maximizers at fixed a and justify passage of maxima to the limit. The limiting stationarity relation gives the claimed closed form; evaluation at t=a and the bound 1 prove the endpoint limit for both profiles. The implicit derivative is nonzero at the a=0 stationary point s=1, giving the stated quadratic error after the first derivative 4/e^2. The monomial checks give beta_2(0)=4/(3 sqrt(3)) and beta_3(0)=3/4. The supplied checker was inspected, not executed.

evidence: Baranov–Kayumov–Nasyrov prove a lower bound about 0.695356 for general finite Blaschke products and give the 2/e monomial obstruction. Dubinin gives a sharp pointwise upper bound at a fixed |f(z)| for products with critical values bounded by lambda, using Chebyshev–Blaschke (Zolotarev) comparison functions. Kraus–Roth optimize a derivative at prescribed critical points rather than a global Bloch supremum.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A universal lower bound does not yield the a-dependent infimum; a sharp upper bound in the full bounded-critical-value class has different equality functions and does not give a finite-degree maximizing radius or degree envelope in the unicritical subclass. The degree-two overlap in admissible class does not extend this to every degree.

value.rationale: The exact degree-uniform lower bound for fixed critical-value modulus quantifies how the monomial obstruction changes under a natural invariant rather than just re-evaluating a monomial. Strict degree ordering, a unique radial optimum and finite-degree equality locations make the result useful for comparing Blaschke configurations within this distinguished class.
